results.corrected_extracted: Two New York State school panels: 5,468 public high-school students linked between fall 1971 and spring 1972 (5–6 months) and 985 graduated seniors re-contacted 5–9 months after graduation (winter 1972–1973). Linkage by self-generated codes matched 66% of fall students in the spring (60% of seniors); unmatched students included more people who used drugs. Each wave was weighted for the selection probabilities of schools and homerooms and for school response rates; the only correction described for unmatched cases is a weighting of the panel to reproduce first-wave marihuana use in the full cross-sectional sample.
results.corrected_locator: Running text, 3rd paragraph (p. 912, middle column); Table 2 caption (p. 913, for winter 1972–1973); References and Notes, note 4 (p. 914)
results.note: All numbers confirmed (5,468 = 66.6% of 8,206; 985; 66%; 60%). 'Weighted only' overstates: note 4 also weights each wave for selection and school response. The winter 1972–1973 date comes from the Table 2 caption (p. 913).

Every value, study count and Z matches Tables 2–6 on 300-dpi renders. 'None significant' refers to pooled means. Expectancy effects on mood and physiological arousal were significantly heterogeneous (chi-square 22.38 and 16.77, p < .05).
